decision_note: Abronia thesis/published source studies moth pollination, pollen limitation and vestigialization of attractive floral traits. Herbivory is discussed as a possible selective cost and moth herbivory is anecdotal rather than a measured focal antagonist response; exclude from primary linked evidence.

A_trait: nectar standing crop; sugar concentration; corolla perforation / robbed-flower state
decision_note: Primary Desfontainia study quantifies nectar robbery, floral rewards, visitor behaviour and seed production under pollinator/robber access manipulations. Robbery strongly depletes nectar but does not reduce seed production when pollinators are present; focal plant trait is not independently manipulated.

Primary Lonicera study shows nectar robbers can cross-pollinate directly while also reducing legitimate visitor rates, producing a coupled positive/negative role boundary rather than fixed antagonist geometry.

Primary Ipomopsis experiment artificially varies nectar-robbing rate and measures male/female pollination components plus reproductive fitness. The manipulated variable is robbery intensity rather than an independently declared plant floral trait coordinate.
